name: vco-stage-count
description: 3 vs 5 vs 7 stage current-starved ring comparison (DR-001 Decision 2's open question)
claim: #8 (design-input claim) -- DR-001 Decision 2 fixes the delay cell and leaves the stage count open ("odd stage count (5 nominal; #8 to confirm against the 200 MHz top of band and the power budget)"). Does the 5-stage ring remain the right choice against a 3- and a 7-stage ring built from the same cell and the same bias generator?
methodology: **Measurement topology**: three rings in one deck at one PVT point, one band code and one control voltage, differing ONLY in stage count (3 / 5 / 7). Each is built from the same `vco_stage` cell and driven by its own `vco_bias` instance out of the committed `design/netlist/vco.spice` export, so the comparison isolates the stage count and nothing else. Each ring has its own supply ammeter. The three rings share only the ideal supply and ground nodes.

**Measurement criterion**: frequency is measured on a ring node (`c1`/`e1`/`g1`), not through the output buffer -- the buffer is common to all three counts and would only add a constant, and this deck is a relative comparison. The period is four whole cycles between the 1st and 5th rising half-supply crossing after `w_settle` (>= 4 estimated periods of the slowest ring in the deck).

**A ring that does not oscillate is a RESULT, not a runner failure.** An N-stage single-ended ring needs a per-stage small-signal gain of 1/cos(pi/N) -- 2.00 for N=3, 1.24 for N=5, 1.11 for N=7 -- and a current-starved inverter loses gain as its head/tail devices are driven fully on. `t<n>a`/`t<n>b`/`f<n>` are therefore declared **optional**: an absent frequency at a point whose ring node is provably static (`s<n>hi` and `s<n>lo` agree to within 1% of the supply) is recorded as data, and the derived `startup` table counts it.

**Start-up kick**: an identical 50 uA / 200 ps current pulse into the first node of each ring. `.ic` alone is not enough -- a noiseless transient solver can sit on a ring's metastable all-nodes-at-mid DC solution indefinitely, and the 3-stage ring was observed doing exactly that at the fast corner. The kick is identical for all three counts, so it cannot bias the comparison, and it is over ~two orders of magnitude before `w_settle`.

Simulator settings: `.tran <tmax> <tstop> 0 <tmax>` with the window sized in-deck from a calibrated frequency envelope (see the fragment header); `tmax <= 1/(80 f_max)` of the fastest (3-stage) ring. `uic` is NOT used: every bias generator is solved to its operating point before t=0. The control block ends with `quit` so ngspice's batch mode does not re-run the whole transient a second time to service the netlist `.measure` cards.

**REDUCED PVT grid, deliberately.** The three rings sit in the same deck at the same corner, so this is a *relative* comparison whose ranking is monotone in N; the absolute per-corner numbers for the chosen count come from the full-grid tuning record, not from here. The grid is the nominal point plus the extreme-slow and extreme-fast composite corners the 63-point tuning campaign identified, at the two band edges of the control window (the interior of a band adds nothing to a stage-count decision).
Statistical switches: `sw_stat_global = sw_stat_mismatch = 0` (nominal per-corner skew, no Monte Carlo mismatch).
**Limitation -- schematic-level, no parasitics.** Every frequency here will move downward under extraction (#18); the stage-count *ranking* is what this record claims, not the absolute numbers.

band.description: 3-bit static band-select code (B2 B1 B0), all 8 codes

vc.description: the two edges of the fine-tuning control window

grid.description: nominal corner -- the reference point the power line is quoted at
extreme-slow composite corner -- binding for the 200 MHz top of band
extreme-fast composite corner -- binding for the 10 MHz bottom of band
